items.title: 67250_John Collins oral history interview
items.q: And in the band was Fats Novarro Navarro, Kenny Durham Durham... I had recorded with these... This was done in '46. This was called 52nd Street jazz

ctx.x: What about the rest of the audience how did they accept it?

They were very responsive, but he -- Panassi Panaci had enough seats there to kind of disrupt things for her, you know, for a while. But this is how fanatical they were about this. And it was kind of nice seeing Kenny because I had recorded with these, I guess they're all stars at that time. When I came out of the army. This was done in '46. This was called 52nd Street jazz, I believe, and this was a original recording of Kenny's tune "Epistrophy." And in the band was Fats Novarro Navarro, Kenny Durham Durham,…

And as I say, it was the first time I had seen Kenny since then, and during that time as I told you I did so many recordings with Jacquet Jacquet and Dizzy also. As a matter of fact one of them was "Muttin Leg" Mudden-Leg, with Illinois Jacquet Jacquet, and his orchestra. And in that band was Leo Parker and Sir Charles
